candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: recognize changes requiring rapid escalation, coordinate interdisciplinary care, and use emergency response systems appropriately.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — stroke-alert activation and rapid team coordination
candidate.educational_objective: Activate the stroke response promptly when acute focal neurologic deficits are recognized so a coordinated team can complete rapid assessment, imaging, and treatment decisions without avoidable delay.

options.A: Mobilize a coordinated stroke team for rapid assessment, brain imaging, and time-sensitive treatment decisions without waiting for a complete diagnostic workup before the response begins.
options.B: Replace bedside neurologic assessment because the stroke team will determine whether the deficits are real after imaging is complete.
options.C: Delay imaging until all laboratory and specialty consultations are completed so the diagnostic sequence is exhaustive before treatment decisions are made.
options.D: Use the alert only when stroke has already been definitively diagnosed, not when acute focal neurologic deficits are first recognized.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline emphasizes expeditious evaluation and treatment, organized stroke protocols, and immediate availability of a stroke team because reperfusion benefit is highly time dependent. Stroke-alert activation begins the coordinated response when stroke is suspected; it does not replace nursing assessment or require definitive diagnosis first. B, C, and D would create inappropriate delay or misunderstand the purpose of the emergency pathway.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A stroke alert is an emergency systems-of-care activation used to mobilize rapid coordinated assessment, imaging, and treatment decisions for suspected acute stroke before a definitive diagnosis is fully established.
candidate.source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
candidate.source_locator: Initial evaluation and stroke-systems sections: evaluation and initial treatment of suspected stroke should be performed expeditiously; organized protocols and availability of a stroke team speed clinical assessment, diagnostic studies, and early management decisions. Section 4.6.1 further emphasizes initiating eligible thrombolysis as quickly as possible and avoiding unnecessary diagnostic delays.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
candidate.stem: A hospitalized client suddenly develops facial droop, arm weakness, and aphasia. The nurse activates the facility stroke alert. What is the main purpose of this activation?
